PullRequest.Title: sessions: fix mobile Back and nested sheet dismissal
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fixes two issues found in the mobile Agents usability audit: browser Back closes the drawer beneath Sort/Actions instead of the sheet, and Escape closes both nested computer-picker sheets.

- Register shared mobile sheets with the workbench-owned navigation stack through a presentation-free contract.
- Keep one history guard while layers are open. Back dismisses the top layer; UI dismissal, rapid replacement, reload, and stale Forward navigation do not consume unrelated layers.
- Let only the top sheet handle Escape and coordinate focus restoration across nested/replaced sheets.
- Reuse the shared sheet shell for Sort, preserving grouped choices and selection semantics while giving Close a touch-sized target.

No session/provider state, desktop presentation selection, or mobile package policy is changed.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp -- compile-client` — passed, zero errors.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/mobileNavigationStack.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/mobile/mobilePickerSheet.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewPane.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionsSignInDialog.test.ts --browser chromium` — 45 passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/mobileNavigationStack.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/mobile/mobilePickerSheet.test.ts` — 19 passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed, including layer type checking.
- Normal pre-commit hygiene and `git diff --cached --check` — passed.
- A temporary Chromium component probe using native Back/Forward/Escape — passed for Sort above the drawer, nested sheets, immediate replacement, and stale Forward. The reload-history regression failed before its fix and passes afterward.
- `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" npm run bundle-mobile` — passed for `8bbb9ac55a94c202293640b93d41f1e46c171f06`.

Two independent read-only reviews completed. No remaining confirmed blocking finding. Physical iOS/Safari, screen readers, and hardware Back are not validated.

## Manual checks

1. In mobile Agents, open the Sessions drawer and Sort. Press browser Back: only Sort closes.
2. Open the computer picker and its nested address sheet. Press Escape: only the address sheet closes and focus returns to its parent.
3. Close and immediately reopen a sheet; Back must dismiss the replacement rather than the underlying drawer.
4. Reload with a mobile layer open, then navigate normally: no orphan history step remains.
5. Confirm Sort selections and a Close target of at least 44 x 44 remain usable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup, reload with an orphaned mobile history guard, and stale Forward navigation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction registers one popstate listener and synchronously checks history state. An orphaned guard schedules asynchronous history.back(); normal workbench startup does not await that traversal. Forward to an obsolete guard schedules its removal rather than reconstructing UI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read browser history state and conditionally traverse back; push a small fixed-shape guard if a layer opens while cleanup is pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup state check; at most one outstanding cleanup traversal. No per-session, per-provider, or per-row operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Startup only attached the history listener and did not clean up an orphaned guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: State inspection is synchronous; history traversal completes via popstate and is not awaited by startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workbench instance and its current history entry; independent of session inventory size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending cleanup traversal per navigation stack; synchronous event handling otherwise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The guard is navigation state, not a data cache. _pendingHistoryPop coalesces cleanup while awaiting popstate; clean startup performs no traversal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and synchronization paths were inspected directly, including reload and stale-Forward coverage.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific history timing is not measured; the new operation is bounded and does not gate initialization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no heavyweight initialization, remote request, or input-scaling startup work was introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Sessions drawer, open Sort or Actions above it, select an option, and dismiss through UI or Back
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening builds the requested sheet synchronously. Sort renders six fixed choices. Selection still waits for the existing 180ms close animation before applying sorting/grouping; Actions likewise invokes only the selected existing action after dismissal. Back now closes the sheet rather than relaying dismissal to the drawer underneath.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize a fixed-size history guard when the first layer opens and rearm it following Back if layers remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One guard for all simultaneously open layers. Nested sheet opens and nested UI closes do not traverse history; each Back with remaining layers rearms once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each tracked part pushed its own state; Sort and Actions were not registered. UI removal of a tracked part traversed back individually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous history operation on explicit user navigation; no network round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update existing storage settings and rebuild/reorder the sessions control after a changed selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selection dispatch, with existing no-change guards; one sorting setting write or the existing grouping writes. No work per option beyond six DOM rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selected ID reached the same setters after the same 180ms dismissal delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing selection processing occurs after sheet animation; the diff does not add another inventory refresh or storage flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch an existing selected action or delegate callback, potentially reaching command-specific external services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the selected action per completed pick, not one action per displayed row. Dismissal invokes no selected action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same action/delegate dispatch and dismissal ordering already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: External command work remains downstream of explicit selection, not sheet construction or Back handling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Six Sort choices; Actions scales with its existing menu rows. Navigation bookkeeping scales with active layer depth, not the number of sessions or action results.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous shell construction and one selected-action dispatch; Actions already prevents overlapping context menus. Shared guard cleanup is coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new data cache. Existing session data and provider state are reused. WeakMap navigation scopes are removed by their owning disposable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the fixed Sort item array, unchanged setters/action dispatch, shell close timing, and history synchronization were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large-session list update duration is unmeasured, but its invocation count and scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the shared shell adds bounded navigation/focus bookkeeping while retaining existing collection work and close timing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Nested sheets, Escape dismissal, immediate replacement, out-of-order closure, and shutdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only the top sheet handles Escape. Closing synchronously disposes listeners, query cancellation handlers, navigation registration, and focus bookkeeping, then removes DOM after the existing 180ms animation. Clear/shutdown dismisses active sheets without reconstructing their content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore one connected focus target, dispose sheet-owned content/listeners, and remove the overlay after animation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one focus restoration per eligible close; bookkeeping scans currently open sheets. One animation-removal timer per sheet, unchanged from the existing shell.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The shared shell already disposed content immediately and removed DOM after 180ms. Generic dialogs separately restored focus after resolution; other shell callers lacked this centralized focus restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Focus and disposal are synchronous during close; promise resolution remains after the pre-existing animation delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active sheet nesting depth, realistically a small number of layers. Closed-sheet history does not accumulate in either stack.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per-window event/disposal handling. Replacement may overlap closing DOM for 180ms, but listeners and navigation entries are already released. Existing search cancellation runs on close.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-window sheet arrays are deleted when empty. Individual entries are removed on disposal, and remaining focus references into a closing sheet are redirected. Navigation scope registrations use weak keys and explicit cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership, DisposableStore cleanup behavior, window-close handling, replacement handling, and nested-sheet cases were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Focus/layout cost depends on browser and content size; no new per-row focus/layout loop or persistent retention was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added state is tied to open-sheet lifetime, and the changed focus/disposal path is bounded by active nesting rather than cumulative usage.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose a computer, replace the picker with Add a computer, open address input or enumerate Dev Tunnels, then connect a selected tunnel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Host rows render from existing filter-service state. Add/address sheets open only on explicit actions. Tunnel rows require the existing authentication step followed by parallel tunnel enumeration and local-tunnel status retrieval. Connecting remains an explicit selected-tunnel operation; Back/Escape only dismisses presentation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire authentication as needed, load the existing tunnel SDK, and enumerate account tunnels through the management client or embedder discovery provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list orchestration per explicit tunnel-list opening, one collection-level enumeration rather than one request per returned tunnel; authentication session creation only when needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical render callback invoked _loadTunnels and the same authentication/listing services on explicit opening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tunnel rows wait for the results, but shell presentation does not. This request is not started by navigation registration, focus restoration, or dismissal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One service call per list opening, concurrent with enumeration and independent of the number of tunnel rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same status query and Promise.all already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Included in the existing Promise.all before rows are filtered and displayed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stage/reconnect the one selected tunnel and await connection through the existing remote-host service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected tunnel per activation, not all rendered hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selected-tunnel connect path and pending host-selection listener existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection gates selecting the newly available host, but is initiated after explicit selection and is independent of sheet history cleanup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H existing host rows and T returned tunnels; enumeration remains collection-level and local DOM rendering remains O(H) or O(T).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authentication precedes the existing two-way Promise.all for enumeration/status; no new per-host concurrency. A selected connection uses the existing connection service. Sheet replacement shares one history guard.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host picker reuses current filter-service inventory. Cold authentication/SDK loading and warm reuse remain service-owned and unchanged. Dismissal prevents late list results from rendering; the diff adds no successful-result or negative-result cache and no automatic retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: sheet entry points, list/connect orchestration, and browser/embedder enumeration implementations were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication/network latency and users' tunnel counts are unmeasured; their request cardinality and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new navigation contract does not eagerly enumerate, reconnect, or repeat remote operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search and drill into remote workspace folders inside a shared picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing picker initially requests results and subsequently debounces typed input by 150ms. Each query loads folder lists for eligible provider actions concurrently, then renders returned rows. Closing still cancels tokens/timers immediately and ignores stale responses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally connect an unavailable provider, then call resourceList once for the queried directory through that provider's connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one resourceList per eligible inline folder action per executed query, not per returned folder. Provider actions run through the existing Promise.all; cancellation can prevent calls or discard late results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial population, debounce, Promise.all, connect-on-demand, resourceList, and cancellation behavior existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Results wait for provider requests, but shell presentation and dismissal do not. No additional call is made by stack tracking or focus restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P eligible inline folder actions per executed query and F returned rows; request fan-out is governed by P, not F.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider requests use Promise.all with no newly added global limiter. Each sheet retains the existing debounce and cancellation behavior; an already issued resourceList may complete after cancellation and is ignored.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already connected provider avoids connect-on-demand; cold providers may establish a connection. Existing query dispatch maps are cleared per query, and no new positive/negative result cache or cache invalidation was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the search callback, debounce/cancellation lifecycle, provider grouping, and actual resourceList call were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count, listing sizes, and network duration are unmeasured, but the diff changes none of their multiplicity or scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the changed shell lifecycle preserves the existing request and rendering path without amplifying boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all nine changed files and all diff pages against base 00ae1a7fa055ef59626d753860a1fd56b529c3ff. Traced navigation history, shell lifecycle/focus, fixed-size Sort selection, action dispatch, tunnel enumeration/connection, and remote folder search. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying performance-regression fix was established. Static read-only review; browser/device timing was not profiled.
